description:
The WHEN OTHER arm of EVALUATE EIBAID at :91-94, driven with PF4. :85 names DFHENTER and DFHPF3 and defaults everything else, so any other key lands here: :92 moves 'Y' into WS-ERR-FLG, :93 moves CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY into the PIC X(80) WS-MESSAGE, and :94 performs SEND-SIGNON-SCREEN, which :149 narrows to the seventy-eight-byte ERRMSGO. PROCESS-ENTER-KEY at :108 is never performed, so the RECEIVE MAP at :110-115 is never issued, the normalisation at :132-136 never runs and USRSEC is never read at :211-219; :98-102 then returns the communication area exactly as it arrived. Note what this arm lacks: there is no MOVE -1 anywhere in :91-94, so no field is repositioned - unlike every other rejecting path in the program, all of which set a cursor.

Why case13 carries this arm. :85-95 is a three-arm ordered EVALUATE whose third arm is a default rather than a test for one particular key, and that is a claim only two cases pressing two different keys can make: case13 presses PF4 and case19 presses CLEAR, and both must land here with the same message, no cursor request and no sign-on. Everything the unconditional fold needs asserting is asserted where it is observable instead, on the paths that actually reach :132-136 - case09 types admin001 and password, lower case throughout, and signs an administrator on; case10 types UsEr0002 and PassWord, mixed case in both fields, and signs USER0002 on from row 6 of the seed with user type U and a response naming COMEN01C; and case16 types USER0003 with a lower-case password, which isolates :135-136 from :132-134. A fourth folding case here would have restated case10 while leaving this arm to a single key, so the arm stays here and the fold stays there.

What the fold is, recorded here because this arm is one of the two paths on which it provably does not happen. :132-134 moves FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(USERIDI) into both WS-USER-ID and CDEMO-USER-ID and :135-136 moves FUNCTION UPPER-CASE(PASSWDI) into WS-USER-PWD, both unconditionally and both after the END-EVALUATE at :130, so on a path that reaches them the keyed read at :215 uses RIDFLD(WS-USER-ID) - the folded value, never the bytes as typed - and the plaintext comparison at :223 tests the stored password against the folded password. Those three receivers are the only ones: nothing is ever moved back into USERIDI or USERIDO or PASSWDI or PASSWDO. Since app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:85 declares 01 COSGN0AO REDEFINES COSGN0AI with the same FILLER X(12) prologue and the same seven-plus-n stride per field, USERIDO at :140 overlays USERIDI byte for byte, so a communication area can carry USER0002 while the screen items still hold UsEr0002 as it was typed - which is exactly what case10 pins. FUNCTION UPPER-CASE folds a through z and leaves every other byte alone, which is why the digits of a key such as USER0002 survive it in place. On this arm none of that runs: EIBAID is PF4, so :108-140 is never entered, nothing is folded, and the area handed back at :98 is the area that arrived. Nothing here may be harmonised with its sibling either: FUNCTION UPPER-CASE occurs twice in app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl and zero times in app/cbl/COUSR01C.cbl, the user-add screen, which stores what was typed. Both behaviours coexist in the legacy system and both are preserved exactly as they are.

USERIDO and PASSWDO are LOW-VALUES, and by derivation rather than by convention. COSGN0AI is WORKING-STORAGE brought in by COPY COSGN00 at :50 with no VALUE clause, so a task that never receives a map still holds binary zeros there; :77-78 clears WS-MESSAGE and ERRMSGO alone, and the MOVE LOW-VALUES TO COSGN0AO at :81 belongs to the EIBCALEN = 0 arm, which this case is not on. Neither item is a payload member: within each field the input view spends xxxL plus xxxF plus a four-byte FILLER - seven bytes - exactly where the output view spends a three-byte FILLER plus xxxC, xxxP, xxxH and xxxV, so xxxI and xxxO occupy the same bytes at the same width, and the program only ever reads USERIDI at :118 and :132 and PASSWDI at :123 and :135, repositioning the cursor through the length items. What the terminal receives here is therefore eight X'00' bytes in each of those two fields, at the PIC X(8) width app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:140 and :146 declare; SignOnResponse carries neither item as a payload member, so the JSON never echoes a credential.

The line that is sent, and the two literals that are not. :93's sender is CCDA-MSG-INVALID-KEY, which app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy:20-21 declares PIC X(50) as forty characters of text and nine typed spaces, padded to fifty; the move puts those fifty bytes left-justified into the PIC X(80) WS-MESSAGE at :38, and :149 then narrows the whole of it to ERRMSGO, which app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:152 declares PIC X(78) - so the pinned value is forty characters of text followed by thirty-eight spaces. Neither thank-you literal is reachable from this arm, and the two of them are a standing trap because they differ in width, in wording and in owner: CCDA-MSG-THANK-YOU is the PIC X(50) of app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy:18-19 that only the DFHPF3 arm at :89 moves, while CCDA-THANK-YOU is the PIC X(40) of app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy:23-24 and names CCDA where the other names CardDemo. expectedMessages is empty by derivation rather than by omission: SEND MAP is not a line - its payload is the map's fields, recorded here as a screen send - and app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl carries no DISPLAY on any path, so the eighty-byte WS-MESSAGE channel belongs to case12 alone.

USRSEC is seeded from app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44, whose ten in-stream rows are 57 characters where app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy:17-23 declares 80: SEC-USR-ID X(08) at 0, SEC-USR-FNAME X(20) at 8, SEC-USR-LNAME X(20) at 28, SEC-USR-PWD X(08) at 48, SEC-USR-TYPE X(01) at 56 - which is 57 - then the named SEC-USR-FILLER X(23) at 57, which is 80. The 23-byte shortfall is supplied once at seed time by the declared USRSEC_FILLER_PAD_57_TO_80 normalisation and never hand-padded, and the 80-character expectedFinalState images prove that span was emitted as 23 spaces - a record missing it would be short by exactly 23. Row 6, the USER0002 row, additionally names all six fields individually so those offsets are diffable against the copybook rather than inferred from one long string: AJITH and KUMAR are the seed data as DUSRSECJ.jcl:41 writes them, each right-space-padded to its PIC X(20), SEC-USR-TYPE is the single U that :227 would move into CDEMO-USER-TYPE on a sign-on path, and SEC-USR-FILLER is the twenty-three spaces that bring the record to eighty. That row is chosen because it is the row a folded UsEr0002 addresses - case10's row - so the shape this arm leaves untouched is stated here at full field resolution. The same job corroborates the target width twice, with DCB=(LRECL=80,RECFM=FB) on SYSUT2 at :48 and RECORDSIZE(80,80) KEYS(8,0) at :65-66 on the cluster. The dataset is addressed by its binding key USRSEC - the CICS file name at :39 - and never by a dataset name. expectedWrites is empty as a positive assertion: COSGN00C contains no WRITE, REWRITE or DELETE on any path, and the read at :211-219 does not even specify UPDATE, so it takes no lock and holds no record. expectedReturnCode is 0 because grep -c RETURN-CODE over the program is 0.

Determinism and the two substitutions. POPULATE-HEADER-INFO opens with MOVE FUNCTION CURRENT-DATE TO WS-CURDATE-DATA at :179, so the clock is pinned rather than read: 2022-07-19T23:12:33, traceable to this program's own version footer at :259 and expressed as a fixed local date-time so no timezone can shift it. Through app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy, WS-CURDATE-MM-DD-YY is MM '/' DD '/' YY with YY taken from WS-CURDATE-YEAR(3:2), giving CURDATEO exactly 07/19/22 at its PIC X(8); WS-CURTIME-HH-MM-SS is HH ':' MM ':' SS, eight bytes, moved into CURTIMEO which app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY:122 declares PIC X(9) - hence 23:12:33 followed by exactly one trailing space. Note that width: the sibling COUSR02 map declares its CURTIMEO PIC X(8) at app/cpy-bms/COUSR02.CPY:128 and the two must not be conflated. APPLID and SYSID come from EXEC CICS ASSIGN at :198-204, which has no Java equivalent and which neither application.yml nor application-test.yml binds, so CICSAWS1 and AWS1 space-padded to PIC X(8) are pinned constants standing in for those two calls; all twenty cases use the same pair, and the substitution is stated rather than hidden. The charset is named US-ASCII rather than left to a platform default, and there is no randomness and no wall-clock reading anywhere in this case.

Security posture, unchanged in both directions. SEC-USR-PWD is PIC X(08) and app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:223 compares it in plaintext, so the seeded PASSWORD stays plaintext both in the ten rows this case seeds and in the six named fields of row 6: no digest is computed over it, no random prefix is mixed into it, no credential transformer is applied to it, no bearer credential is minted from it, and no security filter chain exists anywhere in this file. The fold at :135-136 is applied to the password as well as to the user id, which narrows the effective password space, since a password containing lower-case letters can never be stored and matched as typed. That is an inherited property of the legacy design, preserved deliberately and not endorsed; correcting either of them would be a behaviour change rather than a migration. This arm never reaches :223 at all, which is why the posture is stated here rather than exercised.

Two absences worth stating so that neither is read as an oversight. app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl:59 is *COPY DFHATTR. with the asterisk in column 7 - a COBOL comment - so no DFHATTR constant applies to this program even though the symbolic map carries attribute items; and COSGN00C copies CSSETATY zero times, so there is no DFHRED-plus-asterisk runtime highlight to assert on any path, this one included. The red on the error line is a static map property assembled once from app/bms/COSGN00.bms:197-200, where ERRMSG is declared ATTRB=(ASKIP,BRT,FSET) COLOR=RED LENGTH=78 POS=(23,1), rather than assigned at run time - which is why the screen send this case pins carries eleven named items and no attribute item at all.

Provenance. Every expected value above is statically derived - by structured reading of app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl cross-checked against app/cpy/CSUSR01Y.cpy for the record layout, app/cpy/COCOM01Y.cpy for the communication area, app/cpy/COTTL01Y.cpy and app/cpy/CSMSG01Y.cpy and app/cpy/CSDAT01Y.cpy for the literals and the header, app/cpy-bms/COSGN00.CPY with app/bms/COSGN00.bms for the screen field shapes, app/csd/CARDDEMO.CSD:378 for transaction CC00, and app/jcl/DUSRSECJ.jcl:35-44 for the ten seed rows. It was never captured from a live COBOL execution, which is empirically impossible in this environment: there is no z/OS or CICS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler disabled, no Language Environment CEE services exist, and DFHAID, DFHBMSCA and DFHATTR are absent from the repository. Only the provenance of the expected values is substituted; the twenty cases, the field-for-field diffing and the diff-count-equals-zero gate all stand.

The unit is SignOnService, driven as a plain object with a fixture-backed SecUserRepository, and the eleven-field screen is projected by SignOnController, also a plain object - no MockMvc, no HTTP, no servlet container and no JobLauncher in the path. All conversation state - the communication area, the attention identifier and the two typed fields - travels in the payload, so no server-side session exists to hold any of it, and one payload handed to two independently constructed services must produce one outcome. Neither the backward-GO TO restructuring gate nor the abend gate applies: grep -c "GO TO" and grep -c CEE3ABD over app/cbl/COSGN00C.cbl are both 0, and neither is faked. DUPKEY, DUPREC and ENDFILE are unreachable from this program - the only outcomes :221 can see are 0, 13 and other - and none of them is invented here.
